item.title: Pairing from anti-Hund's coupling under infinite Hubbard repulsion
item.description: arXiv:2611.33286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electron-phonon coupling is a natural source of superconductivity, but in strongly correlated materials the phonon-mediated interaction is often much weaker than the on-site Hubbard repulsion $U$. Whether, and how, it can still produce pairing when $U$ dominates is a basic open question. We address this question by studying a minimal model with an anti-Hund's coupling $J_A$: an on-site spin exchange between two orbitals or two valleys, mediated by optical phonons, that favors a local inter-orbital spin singlet. In the limit $U=+\infty$, the two-orbital Hubbard model on the triangular lattice, doped away from the insulator at $n=2$ electrons per site, reduces to a four-flavor $t$-$J_A$ model. Density-matrix renormalization group calculations find robust pairing throughout $1\le J_A/|t|\le10$, with the largest pairing gap at $J_A\sim|t|$. The Cooper pairs reside on bonds and do not come from a direct attraction provided by $J_A$, since infinite $U$ excludes on-site pairs from the Hilbert space. For $J_A\gg|t|$, the normal state is a second Fermi liquid whose small Fermi surface violates the perturbative Luttinger theorem, and a strong-coupling expansion in $t/J_A$ provides a controlled effective theory of superconductivity from this unconventional metal. Our results provide strong evidence for a strongly coupled superconductor beyond BCS theory, driven by the interplay of the kinetic energy, the phonon-mediated anti-Hund's coupling, and the strong Hubbard $U$. Finally, we discuss possible applications to magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene.
item.dc:creator: Donggyu Kim, Ya-Hui Zhang

item.title: Spin-Wave Excitations in $\mathrm{La_3Ni_2O_7}$: A Dynamical Mean-Field Theory and Bethe-Salpeter Equation Study
item.description: arXiv:2611.33298v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We perform a dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) + Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE) study of collective spin excitations in $\mathrm{La_3Ni_2O_7}$, using a bilayer two-orbital Kanamori-Hubbard model derived from density functional theory. Our DMFT calculations reveal a double spin-stripe ground state. On this basis, we apply the BSE to compute the lattice transverse spin susceptibility, which exhibits a damped spin-wave spectrum with a bandwidth of $\sim$0.1 eV and a wave vector of ($\pi$/2, $\pi$/2), in good agreement with resonant inelastic x-ray scattering and inelastic neutron scattering data. We inspect the orbital-resolved bare susceptibility that provides insight into the momentum dependence of the spin-wave line shape. Further analysis of the irreducible vertex reveals notable frequency dependence in the $d_{z^2}$ orbital. Finally, we investigate the evolution of the spectrum with varying Hund's coupling and electron fillings. Our study bridges the localized and itinerant descriptions of spin excitations in $\mathrm{La_3Ni_2O_7}$.
item.dc:creator: Zhihui Luo, Zhong-Yi Xie, Cui-Qun Chen, W\'ei W\'u, Dao-Xin Yao

item.title: Exact high-order spectral moments and moment-based reconstruction of polaron spectra at finite temperature for arbitrary linear electron-phonon coupling
item.description: arXiv:2611.33431v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a family of exact and efficient recurrence relations for the frequency moments of the single-electron addition spectral function of a generic single-band electron-phonon Hamiltonian with linear coupling to harmonic phonons. Working in the limit of zero carrier density, the formulation applies at zero and finite temperature and generalizes to arbitrary dimensions and lattice geometry. Using the Holstein and Peierls models coupled to Einstein and dispersive phonons as examples, we obtain closed-form expressions for moments of far higher order than those available in the literature, at modest computational cost. Beyond providing stringent benchmarks for numerical methods and experimental spectra, the high-order moments serve as input to approximate reconstructions of polaron spectra at weak-to-intermediate coupling and low temperature. The resulting spectral functions are exact in the weak-coupling and atomic limits, and respect rigorous bounds on the polaron energy and weight that we show the self-consistent Born approximation violates throughout the coupling-adiabaticity plane. The approach therefore offers an inexpensive yet accurate approximation, especially for unexplored or numerically intractable models, before computationally demanding exact methods are applied.
item.dc:creator: Jeet Shannigrahi, Mona Berciu

item.title: Controlling truncation errors in loop tensor network renormalization
item.description: arXiv:2611.33807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: At finite bond dimension $\chi$, tensor network renormalization (TNR) of a critical model eventually becomes gapped. For LoopTNR with $O(2)$ symmetry on the $c=1$ critical line of the six-vertex model, parametrized by the Luttinger parameter $K$, we show that the correlation length $\xi$ of the gapped phase is set by the seed of the dimerization injected by the truncation, and depends on $\chi$ only through it. Read from a weak-coupling window early in the same run, the seed predicts $\xi=10^3$-$10^{16}$ via the sine-Gordon mass-coupling relation with no free parameter, to within a few percent for $K\le1.5$ and about 10% at $K=1.75$; since the seed fluctuates strongly with $\chi$, $\xi$ is not monotonic in $\chi$. An alternation of the vertex weights shifts the seed; with its sign read from a $\pi$ twist, one short calibration predicts a counterterm that delays the breakdown in 16 of the 17 compensated groups of a campaign fixed in advance. A correction of the coarse-grained tensors, repeated during the flow, keeps the runs at $K=1$ and $1.5$ critical up to step 160, the last step computed, and exposes the marginal truncation error that remains. Our findings illustrate a systematic procedure for controlling the relevant truncation error, and thereby extending the critical window, in tensor network renormalization at finite bond dimension.
item.dc:creator: Rikuto Fushio, Kokin Cho, Yuta Yamamoto, Akira Otsuki, Masahito Yamazaki

item.title: Spin-vibronic order in Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$
item.description: arXiv:2611.33814v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strong spin-orbit coupling in $5d$ ions produces multipolar orders that conventional probes barely detect. In cubic $5d^1$ double perovskites, the spin-orbit quartet couples to Jahn-Teller vibrations, and resonant inelastic x-ray scattering (RIXS) has established the resulting spin-orbit-lattice entangled (vibronic) states [Phys. Rev. Lett. \textbf{133}, 036501 (2024)]. We proposed that these vibronic states order cooperatively and thereby explain the hidden quadrupole and canted magnetic phases of Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$ [Phys. Rev. B \textbf{107}, L220404 (2023)], but that proposal rested on a simplified model. Here, we show that a spin-vibronic Hamiltonian derived from first principles, with a single scale factor for the elastic coupling, reproduces the ordered phases of Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$ with the same vibronic states that describe its RIXS spectra. With this factor bringing the quadrupolar transition to 34.7 K, near the measured 33 K, the theory predicts the magnetic transition at 19.3 K, against the measured 18 K, and reproduces the antiferro distortion and the ferro elongation between the transitions. These results support spin-vibronic order in Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$ and point to it as the origin of the hidden multipolar phases of $5d^1$ double perovskites.
item.dc:creator: Zhishuo Huang, Takumi Gengo, Teruki Matsuzaki, Liviu F. Chibotaru, Naoya Iwahara

item.title: Chiral Domain-Wall Modes in Topological Adaptive Quantum Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.33328v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum dynamical systems driven by both unitary evolution and measurements open a new landscape of nonequilibrium phases of matter. The role of topology in enriching this landscape remains less understood than that of entanglement and symmetry. A particularly interesting question concerns protected dynamical modes localized on spacetime domain walls between topologically distinct dynamical phases. These dynamical topological domain-wall modes (DTDMs) are well understood only for $0+1$D walls in $1+1$D fermionic dynamics. In this work, we study $1+1$D topological domain walls in $2+1$D charge-conserving free-fermion dynamics, modeled by topological adaptive circuits that steer the two sides of each wall toward a Chern insulator and a trivial insulator through measurements and feedforward corrections. Although the circuits target no particular wall state, each wall hosts $1+1$D chiral DTDMs. At long times in each quantum trajectory, they exhibit logarithmic scaling of entanglement and charge variance and algebraically decaying density correlations, surprisingly consistent with the ground state of a $1+1$D chiral free-fermion conformal field theory. This contrasts with purely $1+1$D charge-conserving free-fermion dynamics, which exhibits only area-law entanglement at finite measurement rates. We also show that the chiral DTDMs exhibit slow purification dynamics. When the system starts from a maximally mixed state, the DTDMs' entropy decays algebraically, accompanied by a vanishing Lyapunov gap, whereas each domain purifies on an $\mathcal{O}(1)$ timescale. Finally, we propose a physical picture for the long-time behavior of the DTDMs by treating the adaptive circuit model as a quantum cooling algorithm. Our results show that topological phases of adaptive dynamics can protect chiral modes on spacetime domain walls against repeated wavefunction collapse and Born-rule randomness.
item.dc:creator: Asadullah Bhuiyan, Haining Pan, Chao-Ming Jian

item.title: Identifying Renormalization Group Interfaces of Massless WZW Flows $\widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_k \to \widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_1$
item.description: arXiv:2611.33354v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A renormalization-group interface encodes how a flow relates operators at short and long distances. We identify this interface up to topological dressing for the conjectured massless $\widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_k \to \widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_1$ Wess-Zumino-Witten flows at every odd level $k\geq 3$. Global $SU(2)$ symmetry requires the interface to preserve a diagonal current algebra at level $k+1$, built from the currents on its two sides. The $\mathbb{Z}_2$ center symmetry then selects which representation labels the interface. This identification predicts distinct patterns of low-lying interface excitations for flows to the same infrared fixed point. Spin-chain calculations reproduce these patterns for $k=3$ and $5$, providing independent evidence for both conjectured flows.
item.dc:creator: Yuma Furuta, Yuya Kusuki, Toshiki Onagi, Yin Tang

item.title: Spectroscopic Signatures of Polaronic Density Wave Fluctuations in Superconducting Bismuthates
item.description: arXiv:2611.33422v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The bismuthate high-temperature superconductors have been identified as potential bipolaron systems, where hole pairs are bound to local breathing distortions of the BiO$_6$ octahedra in their metallic phase. However, obtaining definitive evidence for these quasiparticles and their excitations remains challenging. Here, we report on periodic modulations of the spectral intensities and scattering rates of quasiparticles on the Fermi surfaces of doped bismuthates Ba$_{1-x}$K$_x$BiO$_3$ and BaPb$_{1-y}$Bi$_y$O$_3$, which are reminiscent of ``hot spot'' patterns that have been observed in cuprate superconductors. We show that these features can be well described by a model where electrons couple to fluctuating density wave modulations with short-range coherence along a $(\pi,\pi,\pi)$-oriented wavevector. The results are consistent with the existence of a two-component fluid where unpaired electrons interact with a fluctuating density wave created by residual bipolarons and their breathing distortions of the BiO$_6$ octahedra.

item.title: Machine-Learning Spin-Fermion Models for Strongly Disordered Magnets: Sb-Doped MnTe
item.description: arXiv:2611.33544v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Metallic altermagnets are promising for spintronics, but most altermagnets are insulating. Doping can induce metallicity, but introduces chemical and magnetic disorder that is challenging to model from first principles. Here, we introduce a machine-learning approach that renormalizes first-principles calculations onto disordered spin-fermion models. The learned models accurately reproduce first-principles magnetic and electronic properties and enable predictions of millions of inequivalent long-range exchange couplings in large disordered supercells. Applied to Sb-doped MnTe, the approach shows that altermagnetism persists up to about 25\% Sb, and reveals disorder broadening as a new factor controlling spin selectivity. More broadly, our work opens a route to combining renormalization with machine-learned Hamiltonians for strongly disordered materials.
item.dc:creator: Do Hoon Kiem, Parul R. Raghuvanshi, David S. Parker, Lucas Lindsay, Valentino R. Cooper, Tom Berlijn

item.title: Unified preparation of exact and asymptotic quantum many-body scars from Dicke states
item.description: arXiv:2611.33987v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a unified quantum algorithm for preparing exact and asymptotic quantum many-body scar (QMBS) states in the spin-1 {\it XY}, domain-wall-conserving, and Onsager scar models. Model-dependent isometries map the exact scar states to Dicke states and the target asymptotic QMBS states to gapless magnon excitations of the spin-1/2 ferromagnetic Heisenberg chain. Exact QMBS states are prepared by applying the inverse isometries to Dicke states. For asymptotic QMBS states, block encoding first prepares the magnon excitations from Dicke states to a prescribed fidelity, after which the inverse isometries map the prepared states back to the physical chains. At fixed target fidelity, the block-encoding success probability has a positive lower bound independent of system size and scar index, implying that a constant number of amplitude amplification rounds suffices. Our algorithm enables systematic studies of nonergodic dynamics on programmable quantum simulators.
item.dc:creator: Yuki Asari, Masaya Kunimi, Tetsuro Nikuni

item.title: Wannier-Based Low-Energy Electronic Structure Analysis of $\lambda$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$
item.description: arXiv:2611.34000v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The low-energy electronic structures of $\lambda$-(BETS)$_2$GaCl$_4$ and $\lambda$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$ were investigated using density functional theory (DFT) and maximally localized Wannier functions (MLWFs). For $\lambda$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$, DFT-selected and directly XRD-refined structural models were compared before and after fixed-lattice relaxation. Their initially different near-Fermi-level electronic structures become similar after relaxation. Relative to BETS, relaxed STF has a narrower frontier bandwidth while retaining a substantial dimerization energy scale. Two MLWFs were constructed for each selected unrelaxed structure to represent the upper frontier bands, with total spreads of 36.708 \AA$^2$ for BETS and 37.578 \AA$^2$ for STF. The Wannier-derived transfer integrals show a pronounced reduction of $t_{d1}$ from 51 meV in BETS to 6.5 meV in STF, indicating selective modification of the low-energy electronic connectivity.
item.dc:creator: Arifa D. Agustin, Aulia A. Firdaus, Fathan M. Santana, Shuhei Fukuoka, Atsushi Kawamoto, Muhammad R. Ramadhan, Isao Watanabe, Dita P. Sari, Yasuyuki Ishii

item.title: Rotational Phonons Activated by Magnetism as a Key Ingredient of Cuprate Physics
item.description: arXiv:2602.21438v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Circularly polarized lattice vibrations carry angular momentum and can link lattice dynamics to collective responses in strongly correlated materials, particularly cuprate superconductors. Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) reveals ubiquitous quasiparticle "kinks" near ~70 and ~40 meV in cuprates, often accompanied by peak-dip-hump (PDH) features, indicating strong coupling between electrons and low-energy bosonic excitations. However, the relevant phonon modes and the role of circularly polarized vibrations in these spectral anomalies remain largely elusive. Here, we investigate electron-phonon coupling (EPC) in hole-doped infinite-layer CaCuO2 at four selective hole dopings (12.5%-56.25%) using the Strongly Constrained and Appropriately Normed (SCAN) density functional with explicit magnetic interactions. At 25% doping, the magnetic phase exhibits substantially stronger EPC (lambda ~ 0.5), five times that of the nonmagnetic phase, producing kinks and PDH features over 40-80 meV, with self-energy magnitudes comparable to experiment. Oxygen rotational phonons dominate the coupling over 50-65 meV, while breathing modes play a lesser role; the rotational modes emerge exclusively in the magnetic phase. At 37.5% doping, lambda increases to ~1.6 due to strong coupling of low-frequency phonons near the Fermi-surface nesting wave vector, whereas at 56.25%, where Cu magnetic moments vanish, lambda decreases to ~0.4. The rotational modes carry staggered angular momentum that cancels in the unperturbed lattice; a time-reversal-breaking gyrotropic coupling on Cu sites lifts this cancellation, yielding a finite phonon thermal Hall conductivity. Our findings establish magnetism-enhanced EPC as an important ingredient of cuprate physics and identify rotational oxygen phonons as relevant to spectral anomalies, superconductivity, and the pseudogap thermal Hall effect.
item.dc:creator: Yanyong Wang, Manuel Engel, Christopher Lane, Sougata Mardanya, Bahadur Singh, Henrique Miranda, Lin Hou, Sugata Chowdhury, Bernardo Barbiellini, Adrienn Ruzsinszky, John P. Perdew, Robert S. Markiewicz, Arun Bansil, Jianwei Sun, Ruiqi Zhang

item.title: PEPSKit.jl: A Julia package for projected entangled-pair state simulations
item.description: arXiv:2605.19960v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present PEPSKit$.$jl, a Julia package for simulating two-dimensional quantum many-body systems with infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPS). PEPSKit$.$jl builds on the TensorKit$.$jl package for tensor computations and provides high-level algorithms for iPEPS simulations that support both Abelian and non-Abelian symmetries, as well as fermionic systems. This work gives an overview of the main package features, which include support for ground-state, time-evolution, and finite-temperature simulations in systems with different physical symmetries and lattice geometries. These capabilities are illustrated through various examples and technical benchmarks.
item.dc:creator: Paul Brehmer, Lander Burgelman, Zheng-Yuan Yue, Gleb Fedorovich, Jutho Haegeman, Lukas Devos

item.title: Probing spin dynamics in MnSi under pressure by energy-integrated time-of-flight small-angle neutron scattering
item.description: arXiv:2607.07660v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We demonstrate that energy-integrated time-of-flight small-angle neutron scattering can determine the long-wavelength spin-wave stiffness of field-polarized MnSi inside a pressure cell. A forward model maps neutron energy loss and gain into the recorded time-of-flight coordinates, allowing a joint fit of radial profiles in several apparent-wavelength windows to constrain a common stiffness. Ambient-pressure powder and polycrystal measurements reproduce the established stiffness scale of MnSi. At effective pressures of 3.5 and 7.8 kbar, the fitted stiffness spans 43--61 meV $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}^2$ across the measured states and is comparable in magnitude to the scale inferred from the helical wave vector and applied upper critical field. The characteristic SANS ordering temperature decreases from 28.8 K at ambient pressure to 17.4 K at 7.8 kbar. The long-wavelength gradient stiffness alone therefore does not account for the pressure evolution of helimagnetic ordering. These results demonstrate a route to quantitative studies of spin-wave dynamics under pressure on time-of-flight SANS instruments without final-energy analysis.
item.dc:creator: E. V. Altynbaev, D. O. Skanchenko, Zhenhua Xie, Yubin Ke, Yuan Bao, Hui Cheng, A. V. Tsvyashchenko

item.title: Symmetry-protected cubic-touching topological surface bands with tunable singularities
item.description: arXiv:2607.19265v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a class of topological surface bands in three-dimensional topological insulators that have symmetry-protected cubic-order band touching. Within the symmetry constraint, the band dispersion can continuously vary between cubic dispersion, moat band and multi-mini-valley structure with van Hove singularities by adjusting particle-hole asymmetry and anisotropy. Thus, there is a family of tunable density-of-state singularities ranging from power-law to logarithmic divergences. This offrs a versatile platform for engineering strongly correlated phases of matter in topological surface states. We provide an example realization in a prism-lattice tight-binding model of angular-momentum-3/2 electrons.
item.dc:creator: Jingtian Shi, Taylor L. Hughes, Ivar Martin

item.title: Many-Anyon Braiding in Non-Abelian Fractional Quantum Hall Effect with Hybrid Monte Carlo Simulation
item.description: arXiv:2608.17424v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We use the hybrid Monte Carlo method to efficiently compute the many-anyon non-Abelian braiding matrices for different Moore-Read quasiholes braiding schemes. Using both a traditional two-anyon braiding scheme and a newly proposed braiding scheme based on global rotation, we approximate the non-Abelian characteristic length of Moore-Read quasiholes around $2.8$ times the magnetic length. We also apply this method to braiding schemes involving six anyons and explicitly show that the well-known ``even-odd effect'' can be flipped by tuning electrostatic potentials. This phenomenon emphasizes the importance of accounting for all anyons within a non-Abelian system, even if the braiding involves only several anyons locally. Our results are relevant to the experimental realization of non-Abelian physics in fractional quantum Hall and other analogous systems, including the fast-growing field of fractional quantum anomalous Hall states in moir\'e materials.
item.dc:creator: Ting-Tung Wang, Ha Quang Trung, Qianhui Xu, Min Long, Bo Yang, Zi Yang Meng

item.title: Hidden Triakontadipole Order in the Triangular-Lattice Magnet CeMgAl$_{11}$O$_{19}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.04845v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The absence of magnetic Bragg peaks and a broad excitation continuum are commonly recognized experimental features of a quantum spin liquid. The Ce-based triangular-lattice hexaaluminate CeMgAl$_{11}$O$_{19}$ exhibits both signatures, yet its effective model and ground state remain under debate. Experiments have variously suggested a quantum spin liquid, proximate umbrella point, and disorder-suppressed magnetic order. Here we trace these contradictions to an overlooked multipolar degree of freedom, and establish a dipole--triakontadipole XXZ model with $J_{\perp} \simeq 0.65$ K and $J_c \simeq -0.13$ K via precision tensor-network calculations. The resulting planar triakontadipolar superfluid order is hidden from dipolar probes, explaining the absence of a magnetic Bragg peak in neutron scattering. The zero-field excitations separate into a low-energy triakontadipole wave and a broad higher-energy continuum. We further propose nuclear spin-lattice relaxation and spin-current experiments to probe the gapless excitations of this hidden triakontadipole superfluid. Our findings thus offer a hidden-order caveat for spin-liquid searches and provide a new platform for exploring high-rank multipolar physics in rare-earth triangular-lattice magnets.
item.dc:creator: Yu-Bo Liu, Yuan Gao, Zhen Ma, Shufan Cheng, Xinyang Liu, Jinsheng Wen, Wei Li

item.title: Non-Perturbative Resolution of Luttinger's Theorem Violations in Strongly Correlated Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.07933v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Many-body physics faces an apparent paradox concerning violations of Luttinger's theorem in strongly correlated systems. The theorem relates the electron number to the Luttinger count---the monodromy of the logarithm of the imaginary-frequency Green's function $\bd{G(i\epsilon)}$---and, at finite magnetic field, connects the Hall conductivity to the magnetic-field derivative of the Luttinger count via the Streda formula. Luttinger's theorem seemingly follows from particle-number conservation alone, without resorting to perturbation theory, and yet it is found to be violated. Here, we provide a non-perturbative solution to this paradox. We show that the Luttinger integral, which accounts for the mismatch between the particle number and the Luttinger count, is a pure zero-frequency boundary term, which the conventional proof implicitly discards. Hence, violations of Luttinger's theorem do not require a breakdown of the skeleton-diagram formalism, whose validity is independent of the convergence of the skeleton-diagram expansion to the exact solution. This advancement in understanding resolves a longstanding point of contention in many-body theory. We also find that the Luttinger integral is a genuine topological invariant, tied to the Luttinger-Ward functional rather than to the Green's function alone; like the monodromy of $\bd{\ln G(i\epsilon)}$, it stems exclusively from the zero-frequency point where the Matsubara trajectory crosses the branch cut of the logarithm. Correspondingly, the magnetic-field derivative of the Luttinger integral makes the Hall number in topological insulators differ from its Green's-function expression by a vertex correction, itself invariant, which can take fractional values.
item.dc:creator: Nazzareno Africani, Herbert E{\ss}l, Alessandro Toschi, Michele Fabrizio

item.title: Kitaev Exchange and Altermagnetism in the Double Perovskite Sr$_2$CoTeO$_6$: An Ab Initio Study
item.description: arXiv:2611.15152v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Co$^{2+}$-based double perovskite Sr$_2$CoTeO$_6$ attracts attention due to its nontrivial magnetic properties. \textit{Ab initio} density functional theory calculations reveal a substantial ferromagnetic Kitaev exchange $|K|\sim J/3$ between nearest neighbors that, combined with the face-centered cubic lattice, leads to pronounced exchange frustration and places Sr$_2$CoTeO$_6$ among Kitaev materials with moderate Kitaev interaction strength. In addition, Sr$_2$CoTeO$_6$ is found to be altermagnetic with a sizable non-relativistic spin splitting, which can give rise to a transverse piezomagnetic effect and a nontrivial magneto-optical response.
item.dc:creator: Alexey V. Ushakov, Sergey V. Streltsov

item.title: $^{55}$Mn-NMR/NQR study on the kagome metal Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$: Re-examining the possibility of spin-singlet paired state
item.description: arXiv:2611.15693v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$ is a Mn-based kagome metal that has been proposed to be close to a ferromagnetic instability. Recent $^{55}$Mn nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) study suggested the emergence of a spin-singlet paired state below $\sim$10 K. To clarify its low-energy magnetic and electronic properties, we performed $^{55}$Mn NMR and nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR) measurements on single-crystalline Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$. From the detailed NMR/NQR spectrum measurements and the DFT calculations, a quadrupolar frequency of $\nu_{\rm Q}$ = 4.6$\sim$4.8 MHz and an asymmetry parameter of $\eta$ = 0.45$\sim$0.48 as well as the principal axes of electric field gradient EFG for the Mn site were determined. The temperature dependence of Knight shift ($K$) shows a similar temperature dependence of the DC magnetic susceptibility $\chi$ except for the low-temperature region below $\sim$ 50 K where $K$ is almost constant while $\chi$ keeps increasing, which suggests that the increase in $\chi$ at low temperatures is not intrinsic. $^{55}$Mn spin-lattice relaxation rate divided by temperature ($1/T_1T$) is found to be nearly constant, confirming the metallic state of Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$ from a microscopic point of view. Furthermore, no peak in $1/T_1T$ is observed near 10 K, and neither the Knight shift nor the linewidth shows any reductions at low temperatures. These results suggest no clear signature for the spin-singlet pairing around 10 K in Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$.
item.dc:creator: Qing-Ping Ding, Yongbin Lee, Charuni Dissanayake, Yasuyuki Nakajima, Yuji Furukawa

item.title: Reflected entropy and Markov gap in Lifshitz theories
item.description: arXiv:2307.12247v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the reflected entropy in $(1+1)$--dimensional Lifshitz field theory whose groundstate is described by a quantum mechanical model. Starting from tripartite Lifshitz groundstates, both critical and gapped, we derive explicit formulas for the R\'enyi reflected entropies reduced to two adjacent or disjoint intervals, directly in the continuum. We show that the reflected entropy in Lifshitz theory does not satisfy monotonicity, in contrast to what is observed for free relativistic fields. We analytically compute the full reflected entanglement spectrum for two disjoint intervals, finding a discrete set of eigenvalues which is that of a thermal density matrix. Furthermore, we investigate the Markov gap, defined as the difference between reflected entropy and mutual information, and find it to be universal and nonvanishing, signaling irreducible tripartite entanglement in Lifshitz groundstates. We also obtain analytical results for the reflected entropies and the Markov gap in $2 + 1$ dimensions. Finally, as a byproduct of our results on reflected entropy, we provide exact formulas for two other entanglement-related quantities, namely the computable cross-norm negativity and the operator entanglement entropy.
item.dc:creator: Cl\'ement Berthiere, Bin Chen, Hongjie Chen

item.title: Tripartite entanglement dynamics following a quantum quench
item.description: arXiv:2408.12533v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the dynamics of multipartite entanglement after quenches from initial states which generate multiplets of quasiparticle excitations beyond the usual pair structure. We focus on the dynamics of tripartite entanglement through the lens of the Markov gap -- a computable quantity that signals irreducible tripartite entanglement when positive. In the tight-binding chain, we show that the Markov gap is positive at intermediate times, implying the presence of tripartite entanglement. After a time delay, the Markov gap increases and then decays at longer times, thus exhibiting an entanglement barrier. We argue that those qualitative features are consistent with an interpretation of the spreading of tripartite entanglement by triplets of tripartite-entangled quasiparticles.
item.dc:creator: Cl\'ement Berthiere

item.title: Genuine multientropy, dihedral invariants and Lifshitz theory
item.description: arXiv:2509.00593v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Multi-invariants are local-unitary invariants of state replicas introduced as potential probes of multipartite entanglement and correlations in quantum many-body systems. In this paper, we investigate two multi-invariants for tripartite pure states, namely multientropy and dihedral invariant. We compute the (genuine) multientropy for Lifshitz groundstates, and obtain its analytical continuation to noninteger values of R\'enyi index. We show that the genuine multientropy can be expressed in terms of mutual information and logarithmic negativity, a relation that also holds for stabilizer states. For general tripartite pure states, we demonstrate that dihedral invariants are related to R\'enyi reflected entropies. In particular, we show that the dihedral permutations of replicas are equivalent to the reflected construction, or alternatively to the realignment of density matrices.
item.dc:creator: Cl\'ement Berthi\`ere, Paul Gaudin

item.title: The Classification of 3+1d Symmetry Enriched Topological Order
item.description: arXiv:2509.10603v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We use a 2-categorical version of (de-)equivariantization to classify (3+1)d topological orders with a finite $G$-symmetry. In particular, we argue that (3+1)d fermionic topological order with $G$-symmetry correspond to $\mathbf{2SVect}$-enriched $G$-crossed braided fusion 2-categories. We then show that the categorical data necessary to define these theories agrees with that arising from a fermionic generalization of the Wang-Wen-Witten construction of bosonic topological theories with $G$-symmetry saturating an anomaly. More generally, we also explain how 2-categorical (de-) equivariantization yields a classification of all braided fusion 2-categories.
item.dc:creator: Thibault D. D\'ecoppet, Matthew Yu

item.title: Robust quantum metrology using disordered probes
item.description: arXiv:2604.11635v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Disorder is ubiquitous in quantum devices including quantum probes designed and fabricated for quantum parameter estimation and sensing. We investigate the robustness of a quantum probe against the presence of glassy disorder. We define a disorder marker quantifying the effect of the disorder by expanding the quantum Fisher information in terms of different orders of the standardized central moments of the disorder-distributions. We classify the quantum probes in terms of the possible values of the disorder marker, and analytically show, for a disorder-sensitive probe with identical and weak disorder on all or a subset of the parameters of the probe-Hamiltonian, that the absolute value of the disorder marker exhibits a quadratic dependence on the disorder strength. We derive a robustness scale intrinsic to the probe that competes with the disorder, and provide a prescription for estimating the maximum disorder strength that the probe can withstand from the disorder-free probe-Hamiltonian for a given initial state of the probe, which can be computed without the disorder averaging. We also extend the prescription to classical Fisher information, and provide an operational perspective to the proposed marker in experiments. We demonstrate our results in the case of a single-qubit probe under disordered magnetic field, and a multi-qubit probe described by a disordered one-dimensional Kitaev model with nearest-neighbor interactions.
item.dc:creator: Vishnupriya K., Harikrishnan K. J., Amit Kumar Pal

item.title: Time-Dependent Classical and Quantum Integrability in Sigma Models: From the $\lambda$-Model to the Perturbed $SU(2)_1$ WZW Model
item.description: arXiv:2605.05111v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using the Hamiltonian formulation of the $\lambda$-model with time-dependent coupling, we compare classical Lax and quantum integrability in the isotropic current-current deformation of the $SU(2)_1$ Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) model. From the classical WZW current algebra at fixed level, we derive equations of motion for the coupled left- and right-moving currents and construct a generalized Lax connection whose flatness fixes the integrable time-dependent coupling. Equal-time Lax-matrix Poisson brackets take the generalized Maillet form, and the $r/s$ kernels satisfy the extended classical Yang-Baxter relation. A coupling redefinition and time reparametrization relate it to the $\lambda$-model with local couplings. At level one, non-Abelian bosonization identifies the deformed model with the interacting isospin sector of the chiral-invariant $SU(2)$ Gross-Neveu model. In its exact generalized Bethe ansatz (GBA) solution, the quantum Yang-Baxter equation constrains the time-dependent coupling. In the universal weak-coupling regime, it shares the leading inverse-affine time dependence imposed by classical Lax flatness of the $\lambda$-model. This common weak-coupling equation coincides with the one-loop renormalization-group equation of the static model, with time identified with the logarithm of the UV cutoff. Periodic boundary conditions in the GBA yield the quantum Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov equations, whose solution gives an exact many-body wavefunction admitting a Yang-Yang representation at any nonzero drive rate. In the slow-drive limit, dynamical dimensional transmutation generates an isospin mass gap decaying exponentially in time on the decreasing-coupling branch, while in the fast-drive limit the isospin sector approaches the $SU(2)_1$ WZW UV fixed point. We also compare classical and quantum integrability of higher-level WZW and noncompact-group sigma models.
item.dc:creator: Parameshwar R. Pasnoori

item.title: Norms, overlaps and Yangian descendants for the Haldane-Shastry spin chain
item.description: arXiv:2606.20168v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Haldane-Shastry spin chain is a prototypical integrable model with long-range interactions, notable for hosting quasiparticles with fractional statistics and serving as a discrete analogue of a conformal field theory. Its remarkable simplicity is closely tied to a full Yangian spin symmetry. While the highest-weight states for this symmetry are known explicitly, a systematic treatment of the descendant states, needed for the computation of various physical quantities, has remained incomplete. In this work, we provide a detailed construction of these descendants in terms of the algebraic Bethe ansatz following recent work of Ferrando et al. In the limit of extreme twist, it includes the Gelfand-Tsetlin basis. As an application, we derive product and determinant formulae for norms and overlaps of these states.
item.dc:creator: Yunfeng Jiang, Jules Lamers, Yuan Miao

item.title: Statistical Mechanics of Non-Abelian Learnability Transitions
item.description: arXiv:2608.19325v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Monitored many-body quantum systems can undergo sharp learnability transitions characterized by how much information can be learned by the observer. When the dynamics conserves a non-Abelian charge, such as an $SU(2)$ spin, understanding how the observer learns the total charge remains an outstanding problem. Unlike the Abelian case, where charge measurements on distinct sites commute, the $SU(2)$-symmetric readouts are noncommuting fusion measurements, making learning a genuinely quantum inference problem. We propose a theory of $1+1d$ monitored quantum dynamics with $SU(2)$ symmetry, and show that it can be described by an effective replicated loop model comprised of a replica-pairing field and a diffusive ($z=2$) background sector that carries the $SU(2)$ charge and remains gapless throughout the phase diagram. Our theory predicts that the "spin-sharpening" and entanglement transitions coincide as a single transition, which is supported by numerics. Ordering of the pairing field produces volume-law entanglement and hides the background sector from measurements, leading to a learning time of $t\sim L^{3}$ for the total spin. When the pairing field disorders, the background sector alone gives logarithmic entanglement and a diffusive learning time $t\sim L^{2}$. Our analysis is controlled by a large-loop-fugacity expansion.
item.dc:creator: Ruochen Ma, Romain Vasseur

item.title: Moore--Read construction and explicit monodromies of Laughlin states on Riemann surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2608.19619v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We revisit the Moore--Read construction of the $\nu=1/k$ Laughlin states on compact Riemann surfaces, deriving their conformal blocks from $U(1)_k$ Chern--Simons theory through the CS/WZW correspondence. We compute their explicit monodromies under quasi-hole transport and Aharonov--Bohm flux insertion, and prove that the monodromies associated with flux insertion asymptotically coincide with the corresponding physical adiabatic holonomies. In particular, we prove that the physical $L^2$ metric on the vector bundle of Laughlin states over the Jacobian is asymptotically projectively flat. We also relate our construction to the recently developed algebro-geometric approach to higher genus Laughlin states.
item.dc:creator: Kiyoon Eum

item.title: Realizing Braided Fusion 2-Categories as (3+1)D Mixed-State Topological Orders
item.description: arXiv:2610.03864v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct large families of mixed-state topological orders in (3+1)D, including intrinsically mixed-state topological orders. We realize these theories by relating the data parameterizing braided fusion 2-categories to the strong higher-form symmetries and their anomalies that characterize mixed-state topological order. We focus here on bosonic theories, which include theories which admit an emergent fermion in the spectrum of line operators. Our general framework is exemplified on the lattice, where we present concrete models and identify how the data of braided fusion 2-categories are physically encoded. We then formalize this data and show that every braided fusion 2-category arises from a general construction (decoherence followed by strong and weak gauging) as the category of topological operators of a (3+1)D mixed state, with intrinsically mixed-state topological orders distinguished by the presence of strong higher-form symmetries whose anomalies cannot be realized in any (3+1)D gapped ground state. Notably, we show that (3+1)D admits a new mechanism with no (2+1)D counterpart: intrinsically mixed-state order whose topological operators braid non-degenerately, but which carries a gravitational anomaly.
item.dc:creator: Ryohei Kobayashi, Abhinav Prem, Matthew Yu
